K's words on the newsletter, verbatim, and how the lead read them.

Fri, Oct 23, 2026: "can i make a monthly newletter be hosted on the site for our leaders to collaborativly edit and it goes out automatically on the same date and time (unless edited) to a list of our members (email list given at first and then all new members get added with an opt-out feature)?"

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, asking for designs: "custom newletter designs, for the page that hosts their creation and management (what ever that needs to be), and how they look when received by the receipient."

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, after seeing round 1's four options (A the monthly letter, B the issue with a cover, C the month built from the site, D the bulletin with chess in it): "lets make the newsletter thing much easier to use for now since the rest of the site isnt finished for those complex integrations. for example we wont have tournaments hosted in site yet so will be mannually linking kingregistration tournaments for a couple more months still, etc. also, be sure to help me know where to make picks and choices, and recommendations, etc."

Reading: round 1 asked too much of the site and of the leaders. For now the newsletter page must be as easy as writing an email: nothing on it reads the site's calendar, results, club pages or News, because the site does not hold them yet. Leaders write the words and paste the links themselves, a tournament's King Registration link included. Round 1's fuller ideas stay on the canvas as directions for later. And K wants to be shown, plainly, each choice that is theirs to make, with the option the lead recommends and why. Already decided by K and not open: LCA admins, the president and the media manager write and send it; every LCA member with an email address gets it unless they unsubscribe; unsubscribing stops this list only; no postal address in any email. K is the site's owner; write "K" or "they", never "he" or "his".
flow:
SHARED BY BOTH BOARDS OF THIS ROUND (read this first).

ROUND 2 DRAWS TWO THINGS for canvas page "18 · Newsletter": (1) Newsletter-E, "The simple one, for now", with its part 2: the easiest possible page for writing and sending the monthly newsletter, and the email it sends; (2) Newsletter-Picks, "Your picks": one board that lists every choice that is K's to make, each with its options, the one the lead recommends, why, and where to look.

THE SIMPLE VERSION IN ONE SENTENCE: write it like an email, paste your links, send yourself a test, then send it to the members.

WHAT IT MUST NOT HAVE: anything filled in from the site (no event picker, no results block, no club posts, no News stories, no counts of them); no cover builder; no numbered pieces to arrange; no queue; no chess position; no side panels that open; no drag handles; no per-section locks; no live preview pane that updates beside the text. If a control is not needed to write, check or send, it is not on the page.

WHERE THE PAGE LIVES. In the admin area, as a page named "Newsletter", next to Group email, with the decided signed-in header (Nav-Header-Final) and the decided admin chrome (Work-J), crumb "Admin / Newsletter". It grows straight from today's Group email page, which already has a subject field, a text box with Bold, Link and lists, "Send a test", a confirm step and a send history. The text box is the site's existing one: its tools are Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link and Undo, and nothing else. No photos in this version.

THE MOMENT DRAWN. Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 2:15 PM, signed in as the media manager. The first issue, November 2026, went out on Mon, Nov 16, 2026. The December 2026 issue is being written. The email frames show it as a member receives it on Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM.

PEOPLE are shown by role with initials in a circle, never by name: "MM Media manager" (you), "PR President", "AD LCA admin".

THE SAMPLE ISSUE, December 2026, typed by hand. Take names, places and figures from the decided boards and round 1's boards (Newsletter-A); badge anything invented "Sample data", one badge per frame listing what is invented.
1. A note from the president: three short paragraphs (thanks to the volunteers of the State Championship weekend in Sulphur; what is coming in the new year; an ask to renew and bring one new player to a club night), signed "LCA President". No person's name.
2. Coming up, three lines typed by hand, each: the date with its weekday, the event, the city, then a link the leader pasted. "Sat, Dec 5, 2026 · New Orleans Youth Chess December Meet · New Orleans · Register on King Registration ↗". "Sat to Mon, Jan 16 to 18, 2027 · Ken Ferguson Memorial · New Orleans · run by Downriver Chess · Registers on the organizer's site ↗" (a partner event: never the word Register alone and never a count). "Sat, May 8, 2027 · New Orleans Youth Chess Grand Prix Final · New Orleans · Details on King Registration ↗".
3. Results: "Marcus Landry wins the 2026 Louisiana State Championship" with 4½ of 5, Sat to Mon, Sep 5 to 7, 2026, Sulphur, 64 players, one line of section winners as round 1 wrote it, and a pasted link "Full results ↗".
4. From the clubs: three short lines (Picayune Chess Club's quick-rated nights on first Mondays; Bunkie Chess Club on Tuesdays, 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM at the Bunkie Library, ages 8 to 108, free to join; Baton Rouge Chess Club's Wednesday casual nights), plain text with one pasted link each where round 1 had one.
5. Scholastic: two lines for parents on the New Orleans Youth Chess season, which began Sat, Nov 14, 2026.
6. Board business: two regional representative seats are open (Central Louisiana and Southwest Louisiana); draft minutes of the annual meeting of Sun, Sep 6, 2026 are posted for members' comments.
Any web address shown (for instance in the link box) is cut short after the site's name, as "https://www.kingregistration.com/…", and badged Sample data.

THE EMAIL'S FOOTER, as K decided: the sentence "You get this newsletter because you are an LCA member." and three links, "Unsubscribe from the newsletter" (one click, stops this list only), "Choose which LCA emails you get", "LCA on Facebook ↗". No postal address, no slot for one, no mention of one. No "Read this issue on the site" link in this version (it is pick 7).

FIGURES. Goes to 243 members (the real count of addresses on Tue, Nov 10, 2026). Sample data, badged: 2 have unsubscribed; November's report "Sent to 243 · Delivered 240 · Bounced 3 · Unsubscribed 2 · Spam reports 0".

WEEKDAYS (checked; use these and check any other date you write): Sat, Nov 14, 2026. Mon, Nov 16, 2026. Mon, Nov 23, 2026. Tue, Dec 1, 2026. Sat, Dec 5, 2026. Mon, Dec 7, 2026. Sat, Jan 16, 2027 to Mon, Jan 18, 2027. Sat, May 8, 2027. Sat, Sep 5, 2026 to Mon, Sep 7, 2026. Sun, Sep 6, 2026.

THE EIGHT PICKS (the Picks board lists them in these words; Newsletter-E draws the recommended answer of each and shows the other answer small where it says so). Each has a number, a question, its options, the recommended one, a reason, and where to look.
1. Which newsletter do we build first? Options: "E, the simple one" (recommended) · "one of round 1's four (A, B, C or D)". Why: E needs nothing the site does not have yet, a volunteer can use it the first time, and it can be on the live site first. Look at: Newsletter-E, frame A.
2. How does it go out? Options: "A person presses Send, after a test and one confirm step" (recommended) · "It goes out by itself on the 1st at 8:00 AM once someone marks it ready". Why: nothing unfinished can go out by accident, and it works the way Group email already does; "Send later" still lets a person pick the 1st at 8:00 AM. Look at: Newsletter-E, frame A step 3 and frames B1 and B2.
3. What does a new month start from? Options: "The usual six headings, ready to fill or delete" (recommended) · "A copy of last month's issue" · "A blank page". Why: nobody faces an empty page or sends last month's news by mistake. Look at: Newsletter-E, frame B5.
4. How do tournaments get in? Options: "Type the line and paste the King Registration link yourself" (recommended for now) · "A small Add an event form that writes the line for you". Why: it is exactly what leaders do in an email today and needs nothing built; the form can come when the site holds tournaments. Look at: Newsletter-E, frame A's Coming up and frame B6.
5. What does the top of the email look like? Options: "A navy band with the rook and the month" (recommended) · "Plain: the rook and the name in text". Why: it looks like LCA at a glance and costs the leaders nothing, because the site writes the month. Look at: Newsletter-E part 2, frames C1 and C2.
6. Photos? Options: "None for now, words and links only" (recommended) · "One photo per issue". Why: the site's text box does not take photos today, so this is the one option that adds real building; photos can follow. Look at: Newsletter-E part 2, frame C1 (no photo) and the small frame C3.
7. Can anyone read an issue on the site? Options: "Not in the first version; add a page per issue right after" (recommended) · "In the first version" · "Never, email only". Why: the email is what members asked for; a page per issue is worth adding next because its link can be posted on LCA's Facebook page. Look at: the Picks board only (nothing is drawn for it yet).
8. Later, when the site holds tournaments and results, which way should it grow? No need to decide now. The lead's suggestion: keep the simple letter, then let the site fill in Coming up and Results as round 1's option C does, and add option D's Position of the month if someone wants to keep it up. Look at: round 1's boards, Newsletter-C and Newsletter-D.

DRAWN THIS WAY UNLESS K SAYS OTHERWISE (the Picks board lists these under their own small heading; they are not picks): one person writes at a time and the others can read; opens and clicks are not tracked; the weekly Monday "News by email" on the decided News page waits, so the newsletter is the only regular email for now; it is sent from an address at news.louisianachess.org and replies go to LouisianaChess@gmail.com.

COPY RULES ON TOP OF THE STANDING ONES. No em dashes and no en dashes anywhere: ranges use "to". Plain words: a volunteer who has never sent a group email must understand every label, so no trade words (preheader, deliverability, campaign, segment, WYSIWYG, template, schedule as a noun for software). Every button says what it does. Status always in words beside any colour. Gold is never text on a light ground. "US Chess" never USCF. ½ never .5. Times as "8:00 AM". Every date with its weekday.

boards.idea: Write it like an email, paste your links, send yourself a test, then send it to the members. One page, three numbered steps down it, and nothing that reads from the rest of the site.
boards.differs: Against round 1's four options: no cover, no pieces to arrange, no blocks filled from the site, no chess position, no panels. boards.spec:
BOARDS. Newsletter-E.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3400 (aim well under: this option is small on purpose, about 2700 is right). Newsletter-E-2.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3000.

FRAME A, "Creating and sending · the December 2026 issue, Mon, Nov 23, 2026, 2:15 PM, signed in as the media manager". The Newsletter page at 1440 in a browser frame, about 1300 tall, with the header, the crumb "Admin / Newsletter", the page heading "Newsletter" and one quiet line beside it: "December 2026 · Draft · Saved 2:15 PM". The page is one main column about 760 wide, with a slim side column about 320 wide to its right, and plenty of empty cream around them. The main column is three numbered steps, each a white card with a large navy number and a plain heading:
STEP 1, "Write it". A "Subject" field holding "LCA Newsletter · December 2026" (the site writes the month; it can be changed). Under it the message box, the site's existing text box, with one row of six tools in words with small icons: Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link, Undo. The box holds the December issue as typed: the six headings with their text from the flow. Show it honestly mid-work: the note, Coming up, Results, From the clubs and Scholastic are written; under "Board business" sits the grey starter hint "Write here, or delete this heading." The three Coming up lines are plain typed lines, each ending in its pasted link, underlined. One link is being added: the words "Register on King Registration" are selected in the first Coming up line and the small link box is open over them, with the field "Paste the address" holding "https://www.kingregistration.com/…" (Sample data) and the buttons "Add link" and "Cancel". Under the message box one helper line in grey: "To add a link, select the words, press Link and paste the address. For a tournament, paste its King Registration link."
STEP 2, "Check it". One sentence: "Send yourself a copy and read it on your phone before the members get it." One button, "Send a test to me", with the grey words "Goes only to your own address, marked Test." beside it, and under it the result of the last test in words: "Test sent to you Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 2:09 PM." A second, quieter button: "See it as members will", which opens the email on this page (drawn in frame B3).
STEP 3, "Send it". One line: "Goes to 243 members: every LCA member with an email address, one email per address." with the Sample data line "2 have unsubscribed and will not get it." Then one gold-on-navy primary button, "Send to 243 members", and beside it a plain link, "or send it later". Under them: "You will be asked once to confirm. A sent newsletter cannot be taken back."
THE SIDE COLUMN, three small quiet cards and nothing else: "Who is here" (MM Media manager, you, writing; PR President, reading; one line "One person writes at a time. The others can read."); "Past issues" (one row, "November 2026 · Sent Mon, Nov 16, 2026 · 243 members", with the links "See the report" and "Start December from this one"); "Stuck?" with one line, "Write to LouisianaChess@gmail.com".
Count the controls on frame A's page (fields, tools, buttons and links, the header and footer not counted): there must be no more than 16.

FRAME B, "The same page's other moments", six small panels in a grid, each labelled B1 to B6, each drawn as the part of the page it changes and nothing more.
B1, the confirm step after pressing Send: a small window, "Send the December 2026 newsletter to 243 members now?", one line "This cannot be taken back.", buttons "Send now" and "Not yet".
B2, sending later: after "or send it later", step 3 shows two fields, "Day" (Tue, Dec 1, 2026) and "Time" (8:00 AM Central), and the button "Send on Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM"; under it the state it leaves, in words: "Waiting to go out Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM Central · Change · Cancel".
B3, "See it as members will": the email shown on the page in a plain window with two choices in words, "Computer" and "Phone", and "Close". Draw it small.
B4, after it is sent: the page's status line reads "December 2026 · Sent Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM to 243 members", the three steps fold into one quiet line "This issue has gone out and can no longer be changed.", and the report shows five figures with their words (Sample data): "Sent to 243 · Delivered 240 · Bounced 3 · Unsubscribed 2 · Spam reports 0", then "Bounced means the address no longer works." and "LCA does not track who opens an email or what they click.", and one button "Start January's issue".
B5, starting a new month (pick 3): "Start January's issue from", three choices drawn as large radio rows with one line each: "The usual six headings" (chosen, with the word Recommended), "A copy of December's issue", "A blank page"; button "Start writing".
B6, the other answer to pick 4, drawn small and marked "Not in this version unless K picks it": an "Add an event" form with four fields (Event, Day, City, Link) and the line it would write, "Sat, Dec 5, 2026 · New Orleans Youth Chess December Meet · New Orleans · Register on King Registration ↗".
Also in frame B, one more small state without a number in the picks: B7, someone else is writing: a banner across the top of the page, "President is writing this issue. You can read it. It opens for you when they close it.", with the message box greyed.

PICK BADGES. Wherever frame A or B draws the answer to one of the eight picks, put a small round gold-ink-on-cream badge reading "Pick 2", "Pick 3" and so on beside it (pick 2 at step 3 and B1 and B2; pick 3 at B5; pick 4 at the Coming up lines and B6). These are in addition to the legend's numbered note badges and must look different from them.

PART 2, Newsletter-E-2.dc.html, "The simple one, as it arrives".
FRAME C, "Received on a computer · Tue, Dec 1, 2026, 8:00 AM". First the inbox line: sender "Louisiana Chess Association", subject "LCA Newsletter · December 2026", then the first words of the note, then "8:00 AM". Then the opened email, labelled C1, a 600 wide message in a plain mail window (From "Louisiana Chess Association", address newsletter@news.louisianachess.org badged "Sample data · from address not decided"). C1 is the recommended top (pick 5): a navy band across the top of the message with the rook mark, "LCA NEWSLETTER" in small letters and "December 2026" set large in white; then the letter on white: "Dear members," and the note signed "LCA President", then the five written sections under plain headings in the kit's heading face, each event line with its underlined link, then the footer from the flow. One column, generous line height, no cards, no buttons, no photo. Draw the whole email, top to bottom, without a cut if it fits; if it must be cut, cut the middle and mark it.
Beside C1, smaller: C2, the other answer to pick 5, only the top 300px of the same email with a plain top (the rook mark and "LCA Newsletter · December 2026" as text on white, a thin gold rule under it), marked "Pick 5, the other answer". And C3, the other answer to pick 6, only the Results section of the email with one photo (the hall photo) and its caption under the heading, marked "Pick 6, the other answer · not in this version unless K picks it".
FRAME D, "Received on a phone": two phones at 390 wide with the decided bezels. Phone 1: the top of the email (the navy band, the start of the note). Phone 2: the end of the email with the footer, in the mail app's dark setting.
FRAME E, "After Unsubscribe from the newsletter": the small page "You have left the newsletter", "You will no longer get the LCA newsletter. You will still get emails about tournaments you enter and about your membership.", a button "Undo" and a link "Choose which LCA emails you get". One click, no sign-in, no questions.
Lay part 2 out in two columns: C1 down the left; C2, C3, the phones and frame E down the right.

LEGEND, six notes at most on each board. Main board, among them: three steps and nothing else (write, check, send); tournaments are typed, with a pasted King Registration link; a person sends it, after a test and one confirm step, or picks a later time; one person writes at a time; what the page leaves out on purpose until the site holds tournaments and results; the report without tracking. Part 2: the navy band costs the leaders nothing; a letter, not a web page; no photo for now; one click to leave, this list only.

GREY NOTE: What; Built from; K's feedback applied (quote K's "much easier to use for now" and "mannually linking kingregistration tournaments" in quotation marks, and say what was removed because of them); Open for K: "See the Your picks board: picks 1 to 8."

REVIEW COUNTS (the reviewer lists these): every control on frame A's page, numbered, with the total (16 at most); anything on either board that reads from the site's calendar, results, club pages or News (there must be none); every Pick badge and which pick it marks; every date with its weekday; every link label.

boards.spec:
BOARD. Newsletter-Picks.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 2600, a fixed-width options board. There is no part 2.

TOP. The title strip: "18 · NEWSLETTER · START HERE" and the heading "Your picks". Under it, in large plain type, three short lines: "You asked for the newsletter to be much easier for now. Newsletter-E, to the right, is that version." "Eight things are yours to choose. Each has a recommended answer." "Reply "all recommended", or just the numbers you want changed, like "2B, 5B"."

THE EIGHT PICKS, as eight cards in a two-column grid, in the flow's order and in the flow's words. Each card has: a large navy number; the question as its heading; the options as two or three boxes side by side, lettered A, B, C, the recommended one first with a navy border and the word "Recommended" in a small navy chip (in words, never colour alone); one line starting "Why:" with the flow's reason; and one line starting "Look at:" naming the board and frame exactly as the flow gives it. Where an option can be shown in a tiny picture, draw one inside its box, simply: pick 2, a "Send to 243 members" button against a small clock reading "1st · 8:00 AM"; pick 3, three little page thumbnails (six grey heading bars; a filled page; an empty page); pick 4, a typed line with an underlined link against a four-field form; pick 5, a small navy band reading "December 2026" against a plain top with the rook and text; pick 6, a text-only thumbnail against one with a photo block. Picks 1, 7 and 8 need no picture. Pick 8's card is drawn quieter than the rest, with the chip "No need to decide now" in place of "Recommended", and holds the lead's suggestion as one short paragraph.

UNDER THE GRID, two small panels side by side. Left, "Drawn this way unless you say otherwise": the flow's list, as four plain lines. Right, "Already decided by you": LCA admins, the president and the media manager write and send it · every LCA member with an email address gets it unless they unsubscribe · unsubscribing stops the newsletter only · no postal address in any email.

AT THE BOTTOM, one line: "Round 1's four fuller directions, A to D, are further right on this page. They are ideas for later (pick 8), not something to choose between today."

No Sample data is on this board, so it carries no Sample data badge. No date needs to appear except "the 1st" and "8:00 AM".

REVIEW COUNTS (the reviewer lists these): the eight picks with, for each, its options, which is marked Recommended, its Why and its Look at; confirm each "Look at" names a frame that exists on Newsletter-E.dc.html or Newsletter-E-2.dc.html as finally drawn (open those files and check the frame labels), or a round 1 board; confirm the words match the flow; confirm Recommended is always in words.

revision.when: Tue, Nov 10, 2026, after K answered the eight picks
revision.k_words: all recommended but I like the design concept of allowing for choice, like having the image thing as an option but not default. same thing with screen usage, we can have alot of stuff there but it doesnt necessarily all need to be shown all at teh same time. use of drop downs, other components, etc are nice.
revision.reading: K picked the recommended answer on picks 1 to 7 and left pick 8 for later. K also gave a design rule: simple by default, with choice kept. An extra (a photo, an event form, a plain top for the email) is an option that is off until someone asks for it; the page may hold a lot, but it does not show it all at once; menus, drop-downs and sections that open are welcome. So the three steps stay exactly as easy as drawn, and the extras move behind three closed controls. Where this revision differs from the spec or the flow above, the revision wins.
revision.rule: THE RULE, to hold on every frame: when the page opens (frame A), nothing extra is open and nothing extra is asked for. Every extra sits behind one of three labelled controls, each closed in frame A: (1) "Add", a drop-down at the end of the writing tools; (2) the small arrow on the Send button; (3) "More options", one closed row under step 3. Frame B shows each of them opened, one at a time. The words "not in this version unless K picks it" and "the other answer" go: these are now options that are there, off until chosen. Photos are possible, never required, and never the default.
